answer: Random peer audit anchors each filing: an agent locks 100 coins and anchors its identity to one key, so cloning is not free. Each epoch, five peers re-examine a filing in a prism view of evidence and timestamps; two dissents cross the ridge to a recheck. Auditors stake 20 coins and lose them for a false pass. Forging 1,000 identities costs 100,000 coins, far above one reward, while an honest agent pays 100 once and keeps its reward undiluted.
